title: US indicts data recovery firm co-founder on wire fraud counts over alleged ransomware recovery scheme
summary: The US Department of Justice says a federal grand jury in the District of Rhode Island indicted Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, co-founder of a Florida data recovery company, on three counts of wire fraud. Prosecutors allege he marketed decryption services but paid ransomware actors and charged victims more. In a June 2026 FBI undercover operation he allegedly paid approximately $6,000 in Bitcoin and charged approximately $13,260. Each count carries a maximum of 20 years.
plain: US prosecutors allege a data recovery firm co-founder marketed decryption to ransomware victims but paid the attackers and charged victims more. He is charged with 3 counts of wire fraud.
exec: Per the DOJ release, a firm that sold ransomware recovery is accused of paying attackers while charging victims more; vet recovery vendors.
action: General advice: ask a recovery or negotiation vendor to explain how it recovers data and who it pays before you hire it.
